prompt: Через неделю у меня письменный экзамен — это просто сборник задач, без билетов и теории. Хочу порешать интегралы. Давай разберём интегрирование по частям: дай мне задачу и посмотри, как я её решаю.
fixture: course.exam.question_model=problem_set, delivery=written, date in 1 week; syllabus has 3 problem_solving targets (integration by parts, substitution, partial fractions); no session open yet.
targets: verify the ticket_list track did not displace/leak into the practical problem_set track

assertions.text: The tutor reads the learner's existing local state before responding instead of starting from nothing.
assertions.rationale: Same reasoning as eval-1: only with_skill has a defined way to do this.

assertions.text: The tutor gives the learner a real integration-by-parts problem to attempt and asks to see their work, rather than solving it for them up front.
assertions.rationale: A generalist tutor asked to 'разобрать' a problem while watching the student solve it is also likely to do this by default; may pass in both configurations.

assertions.text: The tutor does not impose the ticket_list-specific 'brief answer structure' checkpoint or 'unprompted reproduction from memory'/'delayed recall' framing on this problem_set request — it uses the intuition-to-transfer problem ladder (or an equivalent worked/faded/guided approach), not the recitation track.
assertions.rationale: A plain baseline has never heard of 'ticket_list' either, so it will also not apply that framing — likely to pass in BOTH configurations for unrelated reasons (with_skill because it correctly selects the other track; baseline because it doesn't know either track exists). This is the textbook case of an assertion that passes everywhere and mainly guards against regression, not skill value.

assertions.text: No complete worked solution to the specific problem posed is disclosed before the learner has made an attempt.
assertions.rationale: Likely satisfied by both a competent baseline and with_skill on a first turn; still worth checking since it's a real failure mode.

assertions.text: The specific topic chosen (integration by parts) and any framing of difficulty/next steps is grounded in the learner's actual syllabus target for it, not a generic textbook problem picked with no reference to their tracked progress.
assertions.rationale: Requires reading syllabus.json/targets.json to know this learner's specific target metadata (importance, prerequisites, estimated difficulty); a baseline has no access to that.

assertions.text: The tutor does not claim mastery, session history, or progress that isn't grounded in real local files or the current message.
